overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting hybrid-meeting notices that implied executive session would occur before any open session, but did not violate it through the non-working Zoom link; minutes amendment was recommended, not ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the January 22 and February 5 notices denied public access to the open sessions that preceded executive sessions, because the notices listed executive session first.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the notices gave the impression that there was no open session prior to the executive session during which the public could witness the procedure to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that on February 5 the Zoom link on the notice did not let him access the open session that preceded executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Because a reasonable reading of the notices suggested that in-person attendance would be the best option for those with a “particular interest” in a topic to be discussed, we find the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We therefore order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
